# Stage 7: Metric library

Define each number goals are measured by once (its meaning and calculation, unit, direction, source and owner), and say which metric measures a goal, for a team or the whole company. The [Metric library module](../modules/metrics/README.md), from its `module.json`.

**Today:** an outline: entry and exit criteria, checked by hand, with no drill yet.

## Entry criteria

- Stages 1 to 3 pass their exit criteria.
- The core’s [module platform](module-platform.md) is built (stage 3): the places, routes, menu rows, Workspace sections, Help and AI tools a module registers into, `Workspace.modulesOff` and Workspace → Features, the sentences a switched-off module says, and the AI tools’ server with its door.
- Undo and Recently removed, Start {next year}, the one-table check-in with its receipt, and History’s second line are the core’s (stage 3, “The core screens the module stages stand on”); the Metric library adds to them through `checkin.number`, `checkin.table`, `goal.measure` and the hooks `afterGoalSaved`, `beforeCheckIn` and `onSwitch` ([the module platform](module-platform.md#what-a-module-needs-that-faros-core-still-draws)). The import (`/data/import`, criterion 21’s Metrics sheet) is Spreadsheets’ (stage 9): until stage 9 is built, the sheet’s rows are proved through the module’s own sheet functions (metrics.csv’s `sheet` rows).
- The core keeps a module’s own records (stage 2): a save carries them with the core’s, in one transaction; the workspace holds them by module and record; a removal saves them as changed, and Undo puts each back as it was just before.
- Goals have a unit (metric and range goals) and teams have ids, so a link can check its unit and slice.

## What to build

The metric library, and the worked example of a module with records of its own. A metric (name, meaning and calculation, unit, decimals, which way is better, source and its owner, refresh, owner, caveats) is defined once per workspace, and a goal links to one metric for a slice (a team, or the whole company), the goal’s own target being the target in it. Anyone adds a metric; its owner or an admin changes or removes it; the goal’s owner or an admin links and unlinks. Every change is logged, removing and unlinking keep the row and come back with Undo or Recently removed, and the AI tools do the same under the same rules. Its two records are its own, not the core’s: the module declares each (what one row is, its table, where a save and the workspace file it, whether it can be removed) with its rows each way, what a new cycle carries over (every metric not removed; the links in force to the cycle’s live goals) and how a removed metric comes back, and the core’s store, removal, restore, cycle and export keep them without knowing what they are. Its rules sit in its own folder, as pure as the core’s. Its own place, /metrics: the library (find by name, unit, owner or meaning; filter by unit, the team or the whole company a goal measures it for, owner, direction, unused, or something to sort out; sort A to Z, by most goals or by the latest change; 50 a page), a page per metric with its meaning, every goal measured by it side by side (status, slice, now, target, against plan) and what it still needs, an item in the menu after People, and the metric on a goal’s page and on a person’s and a team’s. “Measured by” in the goal forms: find a metric by typing (or add one there); choosing it on a new goal fills in its unit, decimals and direction; Goals filters by the metric. Defining one well: three things to be usable, the rest said later and named in words (“Fully defined” or “Still to say: …”, never a score), and three questions answered once before saving (a close name, a unit spelt another way, a percentage that doesn’t say out of what), with each Must fix and Check under its field. For, and which part: a link is for a team or the whole company and optionally one part of that number (“tier-1 services”), the parts in use offered under the field; the goal takes the metric’s unit and direction, its target stays its own; another goal on the same number, or a part spelt like one in use, is asked about once; and a goal with check-ins says why it is measured differently, in its History. Looking after one: what it still needs, a confirm before changing a unit or direction goals use, and on Workspace → About how many metrics have no owner. Measurement status: each metric says whether it is measured today (Measured, Partly or Gap, a shape and a word, with what is missing); a gap or a part is listed under To sort out, and a goal measured by a gap is held to no number (the core’s rule over the goal’s own field, which the library fills in when it links the goal and when the metric is measured). The Metrics sheet in and out: the workbook’s Metrics sheet loads back through the core’s change engine, by a planner the module gives its sheet, with the library’s own rules, the import’s questions and one Undo; it carries the metric’s structure as Part of, How it relates, Confidence and How it could be gamed, refusing a loop or a level with no parent in the library’s words. Metric quality (MQ2): each metric is Draft, Defined or Verified, worked out from what it says, never stored. Defined needs ten parts (meaning; a structured calculation, what is measured and how it is aggregated, with a ratio's numerator and denominator; each part's filters and exclusions; unit; direction; a structured window; the source with a link; the source's owner; refresh; an owner who is here). Verified needs someone other than the owner and the last editor of the calculation to reproduce the figure from the link, and lapses on a change to the calculation, window, source or direction, or after 12 months. Baselines are kept per slice with History. A goal on a metric that refreshes monthly or quarterly checks in monthly or quarterly (the core’s rule over the goal’s own field, `checkInRhythm`, which the library fills in when it links the goal, when the refresh changes and when it is switched); someone leaving passes the metrics they own to their lead to confirm (the core’s `personLeft` hook); and the Metrics sheet takes the calculation, window and source link, its preview counting the stages.

What it adds to the core (routes, places on core screens, AI tools, Help) is in [its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#what-it-adds-to-the-core).

The core also draws for it while it is on, as Faro’s core code that asks whether it is on: `workspace.about`, `afterGoalSaved`, `beforeCheckIn`, `onSwitch`, `goalRhythm`, `personLeft`, `drill` ([what each is](module-platform.md#what-a-module-needs-that-faros-core-still-draws)). A core that never names a module has each as a place or a hook from stage 3; this stage fills them.

It keeps records of its own, which the core stores without knowing what they are: metric (`okr_metrics`), metric link (`okr_goal_metrics`). Every field is in [its records](../modules/metrics/records.md); how the core keeps a module’s records is stage 2’s (`src/domain/records.ts`): declared rows each way, what a new cycle carries, and how a removed one comes back, saved with the core’s in one transaction.

## Exit criteria

1. Its requirements hold: `METRICS-LIBRARY`, `METRICS-MEASURED-BY`, `METRICS-CARE`, `METRIC-DEFINED`, `METRIC-PARTS`, `METRIC-CHANGE`, `METRIC-MEASUREMENT`, `METRIC-STRUCTURE`, `METRIC-SHEET`, `METRIC-STAGE`, `METRIC-VERIFY`, `METRIC-BASELINES`, `READING-PREFILL`, `READING-RECORDED-ONLY`, `READING-SEVEN-DAYS`, `READING-SHOWN` (words in [its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#requirements)).
2. Its journeys and checks can be done: U81, U82, U83, U145, U105, U146, U106, U152, U156, U157, U158, U159, U160, U172, N29, F15, N16, U170, U179, U180, U161, U72 ([its section](../modules/metrics/README.md#journeys-and-checks), where each journey’s Id opens its steps and checks in words).
3. A metric with a name, a unit and a direction saves; without any one of them it is refused with what is missing, and a second metric with the same name (any case) is refused.
4. Only a metric’s owner or an admin can change or remove it; only a goal’s owner or an admin can link or unlink the goal.
5. A goal in hours can’t be measured by a metric in minutes, and a goal with dated stages can’t be measured at all; a goal aiming the other way from the metric’s better direction links, with a warning.
6. A metric that has measured a goal can’t be deleted (“Retire it instead.”); one that never has is deleted, and Undo or Recently removed brings it back.
7. The demo workspace’s 13 metrics and 12 links load (two of them for one part: CI/CD · main branch pipelines, CI/CD · main pipelines), and every goal’s numbers, status and dates are exactly as without them (the conformance rows don’t move).
8. Built without the module, a workspace that holds its rows loads and saves, and none of its rows is changed or deleted; with the module back, they are all there.
9. Starting the next year carries every goal’s metric link to its copy: the same metric, team and part (journey U152; the core’s carry journey, U115, checks nothing of the module’s).
10. The library finds what each of rule 1’s worked examples says, a metric’s goals are rule 2’s rows in its order, and what a metric needs is rule 3’s, in order: every row of spec/conformance/metrics.csv (each search’s and each Metrics sheet case’s inputs are in `module-cases.json`, which the harness puts beside the workspace) matches.
11. The library is in the menu after People (under More on a phone); the old addresses of Metrics under Data lead to the library, a metric or the form; a metric’s row in the library counts the same goals by status as its page’s table lists (journey U81, checks F15 and N16).
12. In New goal, “Measured by” comes first on the measure step: a metric found by typing shows its meaning, fills in the unit, decimals and which way is better on a goal nobody typed them for, measures it for the goal’s team or the whole company, and Check says so; one added there is chosen; a goal with dated stages has none (journey U82, rule 5’s worked examples).
13. Adding a metric with a name close to one in use asks about it and still saves (rule 4’s worked examples); changing a unit or direction goals use asks first (the read-back, MT3); admins see on Workspace → About how many metrics have no owner (journey U83).
14. Adding a metric needs only a name, a unit and which way is better; its page then says what is still to say in words (“Fully defined”, or “Still to say: …”, and “Its owner has left.”), never a number, and every metric in the demo says the line rule 6 gives (the conformance rows `still`). A name a letter or a word from another’s or one a metric used to have, a unit spelt another way, and a percentage that doesn’t say out of what are each a Check answered once before saving, on the form and through save_metric’s checks and answers (rule 6’s worked examples; journey U105).
15. A link takes a part of at most 60 characters; a part spelt like one in use and another goal on the same metric, team and part are each a Check answered once; a goal with check-ins whose metric, team or part changes is refused without a reason, and the History entry gives it; the form offers the parts in use, and a goal’s About lists For, What it means, From the metric, where the number comes from and the goal’s own target (rule 7’s worked examples; journey U146).
16. Changing a metric goals use reads back first (MT3, rule 3): reworded caveats or a new name save at once; a new meaning or source asks “Is it still the same number?”, and “The number itself changes” is refused without a reason, then marks every goal’s chart (“Definition changed, week {w}”, a dashed hairline with its label beside it) and History, which Undo takes back; a new direction needs a reason and marks them too; a new unit is a new label (every goal’s unit changes in the same save) or a different scale, refused. Retiring a metric with goals keeps their links and numbers, leaves it out of the pickers and the library’s list, refuses a new goal it, and says so on each goal; Bring it back undoes that. Admins merge a metric into another in the same unit: every goal moves, the old one is retired pointing to the new, one Undo puts it back; a non-admin is refused (journey U106, rules 3 to 5’s worked examples).
17. A metric said to be a Gap holds every goal it measures to no number in the same save (the goal says Not measured yet and nothing on it is due); said to be measured, partly or in full, or unlinked, the goal is held to its plan again; the library lists the gap under To sort out.
18. A number source reads a metric for a link’s slice (a team or the whole company, and a part) or says it doesn’t, and passes the source contract; a reading’s state in a check-in is rule 1’s (no-slice, unreachable, missing, old after 7 days, same, jump, changed, fresh), and what a check-in records of it is rule 2’s, which nothing that judges a goal reads (the reading rule’s worked examples; the `reading` rows of spec/conformance/metrics.csv).
19. The check-in’s number step (the core’s place checkin.number) opens with a fresh reading in the field, “From {source}, read {when}.” and “Confirm {value} {unit}”; a different number asks why from four reasons before “Use {typed} {unit}”; a reading more than 7 days old is neither filled in nor shown; a company-wide source never fills in a team’s goal; the read-back says where the number came from; the one table fills fresh readings in the quiet ink and asks why in a changed row; and rule 3 (a differing number needs a reason) holds at the form, the table and post_check_in’s reading_confirmed and different_because alike (journeys U156 to U160). With the module off the step is as it was.
20. Where a number came from shows beyond the check-in, from what each check-in recorded: the goal’s Measured by says “This week’s number” from its latest check-in, each History row says it came from the source or was typed over it and why, the metric’s page says for each goal how its check-in gets its number and, over the last 8 weeks, how many numbers filled in from the source were typed over (goals and weeks, never people; rule 4), a review’s agenda says “· from {source}” after a confirmed number, and the Check-ins sheet has four columns for reading that load back as no change; get_goal and get_metric say the same (journey U161). Real connectors are R12’s (spec/requirements/internal/r12-number-sources.md).
21. The Metrics sheet loads back (MI): an export loaded unchanged plans nothing; a row with no ID adds a metric owned by whoever loads it; a row with an ID changes that metric, and Retire with a Reason retires it; a name used twice, an ID that isn’t here and a unit change on a metric goals use are each a Must fix in the form’s words; one Undo puts every row back; with the module off the sheet is said once and not read.
22. A Metrics sheet row whose Part of would put a metric under itself, directly or round a loop, is a Must fix in the library’s words (“Choose another parent: it’s already under this one.”), and an export of a metric with a parent, level, confidence and gaming loads back changing nothing.
23. Metric quality (MQ2): every metric's stage and the parts it still needs are the `stage` rows of spec/conformance/metrics.csv; a Draft metric still measures a goal; the owner and whoever last changed the calculation are refused verifying in words that say who can; a Verified metric whose window changes asks once (lapse: go) and is Defined after, with the reason kept; a reworded exclusion asks its last verifier to confirm and Verified stands; a baseline needs its value, period, day and how, and a new figure for the same period needs a reason; save_baselines and verify_metric do the same through MCP, and refuse with the module-off sentence when Metrics is off (rule 13 to 16's worked examples).
24. Rhythm, handover and the sheet (MQ2 part 3): linking a goal to a metric that refreshes monthly gives the goal a monthly check-in rhythm, with a line in its History, and link_goal_metric returns it (data.rhythm) with a Draft metric's warning (data.draft); a monthly goal is due only in its month's last week and never reads No recent update in between (the core's goal-rhythm rule's worked examples); switching Metrics off puts every goal back on the cycle's rhythm; mark_person_left passes the leaving person's metrics to their team's lead, each to confirm, the stage unchanged, and lists them; the Metrics sheet reads What is measured, How aggregated, the parts, Window and Source link, and its dry run says the stages, similar metrics and each Draft's missing parts.

## Gaps in the kit

- The goals table is where slices side by side and numbers read from the source would grow (growth.md: dimensions an admin defines; numbers from the source).
- Left out on purpose and written down as ways to grow: spec/modules/metrics/growth.md.
- Owner-only rights and other governance, and versions, are left out on purpose (growth.md); draft states are MQ2's stages.
